subject.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally override upstream ACPX cooperative-cancel semantics by closing and evicting the reusable live runtime handle, and should any unverifiable or undrainable stale ACPX lease block backend registration?
rationale: Direct dependency inspection confirms cancel and close are separate upstream contracts; choosing a stronger stop guarantee trades compatibility and startup availability and cannot be authorized by technical review alone.

options.title: Approve fail-closed containment
options.body: Accept destructive cancellation and startup refusal because a successful stop must guarantee no leased autonomous worker remains.

options.title: Add recovery before approval
options.body: Keep the containment model but require a visible Doctor/Fix or targeted quarantine path before backend-wide startup refusal ships.

options.title: Preserve upstream semantics
options.body: Keep cooperative cancellation separate from close and pursue an upstream lifecycle mechanism with less compatibility impact.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed containment
recommendation.body: Accept destructive cancellation and startup refusal because a successful stop must guarantee no leased autonomous worker remains.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available history signal across the current ACPX runtime, process reaper, control-plane cancellation, and abort-feedback surfaces.
